questions.heading: A Convex Cost Can Be Split Into Segments the Solver Fills in Order
questions.stem: A model minimizes a fuel bill written as 2 d1 + 3 d2 + 5 d3 with 0 <= d1 <= 100, 0 <= d2 <= 100, 0 <= d3 <= 50 and fuel = d1 + d2 + d3. A plan needs 150 units of fuel. Which values does the solver return?

options.text: d1 = 50, d2 = 100, d3 = 0, since the middle tier is the widest
options.says: Width does not matter to the solver; it takes the cheapest units first, and d1 at 2 per unit is cheaper than d2.

options.text: d1 = 100, d2 = 50, d3 = 0, since the cheaper units go in first
options.says: Right: minimizing the bill takes all 100 units at 2 before any at 3, which is also the true order of the tiers.

options.text: d1 = 50, d2 = 50, d3 = 50, since the rows treat every tier alike
options.says: That split costs 500, and d1 = 100, d2 = 50 costs 350; the solver returns the cheaper one.

options.text: Any values adding up to 150, since no row fixes the order
options.says: No row fixes the order, but the objective does: only the cheapest split is optimal.

questions.heading: Without Binaries, the Push Must Match the Shape
questions.stem: A maximization adds a reliability value v of crew hours h: 8 per hour for the first 100 hours, 5 per hour for the next 100 and 2 per hour after that, written with one bounded variable per tier and no binaries. Which statement about v is right?

options.text: It needs a binary per tier, since every curve must be told its segment
options.says: A concave value that the objective pushes up is exact with segment variables alone; only the other two combinations need binaries.

options.text: It needs binaries, since a maximized value is pushed upward
options.says: Being pushed up is fine when the slopes fall: the most valuable hours come first, which is the true order.

options.text: It overstates v, since the solver fills the 2-per-hour tier first
options.says: A maximization fills the 8-per-hour tier first, the most valuable one, which is the order the curve has.

options.text: It is exact, since the worth per hour falls and is pushed upward
options.says: Right: a concave curve pushed up is one of the two cases that need no binaries.

questions.heading: The Same Cost Is the Largest of Its Lines
questions.stem: A shortfall penalty p is written as p >= 10 s and p >= 30 s - 400, with 0 <= s <= 50, and p is subtracted from a maximized objective. At s = 30, which value of p does the solver use?

options.text: 500, the higher of the two lines at s = 30
options.says: Right: the solver lowers p until a row stops it, and 30 x 30 - 400 = 500 stops it first.

options.text: 300, the line of the first segment at s = 30
options.says: p = 300 breaks p >= 30 s - 400, which asks for 500 at s = 30.

options.text: 400, the average of the two lines at s = 30
options.says: p must be at least every line, so it is at least 500; an average of the lines is below one of them.

options.text: Any p of 300 or more, since p only has lower limits
options.says: The rows ask for at least 500, and the objective then pushes p down to exactly 500.
